newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian central bank foreign assets rose in July.
newsitem.headline: Latvian central bank foreign assets rose in July.

text.p: The Bank of Latvia, the country's central bank, said on Monday that its foreign assets grew in July and that deposits in commercial banks also rose.
Latvia has been gradually recovering from a banking crisis that hit in the middle of last year.
In its latest monetary bulletin, the central bank said its net foreign assets in convertible currencies rose to 288.5 million lats in July from June's 283.5 million lats.
The central bank's net domestic assets fell to 13.1 million lats in July from the previous month's 27.7 million lats.
Currency in circulation rose slightly in July to 246.3 million lats from 244 million lats in June, the bank added.
The central bank also said the banking system maintained its recovery as deposits in commercial banks rose to 326.7 million lats in July from 314.2 million lats the previous month.

The banking sector's net foreign assets rose to 379.2 million lats in July from 371.6 million lats in June while domestic assets increased to 179.2 million lats from the previous month's 172.8 million lats, the central bank added.
It also said the average interbank rate on credits in lats in July was 11.1 percent versus 11.9 percent in June.
